mainTopic: חמץ mixtures after פסח, the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about חמץ pots, and bread from an oven greased with meat fat
overview: רבא rules that during פסח, even a tiny amount of חמץ forbids a mixture, like רב. After פסח, a mixture is permitted, like רבי שמעון. The גמרא answers a contradiction: רבי שמעון's קנס applies only to pure חמץ, not to a mixture. It then shows that רבא learned this from רב נחמן. רב rules that pots used for חמץ on פסח must be broken, as a גזירה, in case someone later cooks the same kind of food in them. שמואל disagrees and lets the pots be used after פסח for any food. He held back from teaching this publicly only out of respect for רב in רב's town. Finally, רבא בר אהילאי forbids bread from an oven greased with meat fat forever. A ברייתא is brought to challenge him, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's final ruling on חמץ mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the הלכה: during פסח, any amount of mixed-in חמץ forbids the mixture, like רב. After פסח, the mixture is permitted, like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The law is: חמץ during its time (פסח), whether mixed with its own kind or with a different kind, is forbidden in even the tiniest amount, like רב. Not during its time (after פסח), whether with its own kind or a different kind, it is permitted, like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the earlier debates and tells us the practical הלכה for חמץ that got mixed into other food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits the ruling by time. During פסח he is strict like רב: even a משהו forbids the mixture, no matter what it is mixed with. After פסח he is lenient like רבי שמעון, who holds that חמץ after its time is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is (the practical ruling)
In its time, meaning during פסח
Mixed with its own kind (e.g., wheat with wheat)
Mixed with a different kind
With any amount at all, even the tiniest

steps.whatToRemember: During פסח: a mixture is forbidden even with a משהו of חמץ. After פסח: a mixture is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the foundation of the practical הלכה that חמץ is not בטל even in a tiny amount during פסח.

phrases.english: Rava said: The law is
chametz in its time (during Pesach),
whether with its own kind or not with its own kind —
is forbidden in any amount, like Rav.
phrases.notes: Even the tiniest amount forbids the mixture.

phrases.english: Not in its time (after Pesach),
whether with its own kind or not with its own kind —
it is permitted, like Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling on the earlier debate between רב, שמואל and others about mixtures of חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During פסח, a mixture of חמץ is forbidden במשהו in all cases. After פסח, it is permitted in all cases.

steps.title: רבא seems to contradict himself about רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא can say רבי שמעון permits חמץ after פסח, when רבא himself said elsewhere that רבי שמעון imposed a קנס on such חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבא really say this? But רבא said: רבי שמעון imposed a penalty, since the person transgressed 'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא with a different statement of his own, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere רבא explained that even רבי שמעון forbids חמץ a Jew kept over פסח, as a קנס for violating בל יראה and בל ימצא. If so, how can רבא now rule that after פסח it is permitted according to רבי שמעון?

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say? (opens a challenge)
He imposed a penalty
The prohibition against חמץ being seen in your possession
The prohibition against חמץ being found in your possession

phrases.english: And did Rava really say this?
But didn't Rava say:
Rabbi Shimon imposed a penalty,
since he transgressed on it
'it shall not be seen' and 'it shall not be found'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of step 1 (permitted after פסח, like רבי שמעון).
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי שמעון permits חמץ after פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself said that רבי שמעון penalizes a Jew who kept חמץ over פסח, so רבי שמעון does not simply permit it.

steps.title: The penalty applies only to unmixed חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The קנס of רבי שמעון applies only to חמץ that is whole and unmixed, not to חמץ inside a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies when it is in its pure form, but through a mixture, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by limiting the קנס to a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements of רבא are true, but they cover different cases. Pure חמץ kept over פסח is penalized. A mixture is not penalized, so step 1's lenient ruling about mixtures after פסח stands.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only) to...
In its pure, recognizable form
A mixture

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits all חמץ kept over פסח. Pure חמץ that a Jew owned during פסח is still forbidden because of the קנס. Only a mixture is permitted.

phrases.english: These words apply to it in its pure form,
but through a mixture — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּעֵינֵיהּ, אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי תַּעֲרוֹבֶת — לָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קנס of רבי שמעון forbids all חמץ kept over פסח, even in a mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנס applies only to pure חמץ. Mixtures after פסח are permitted.

steps.title: רבא is consistent: רב נחמן's instruction after פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows רבא is consistent with his view. He recalls that right after פסח, רב נחמן told his students to go buy חמץ from gentile soldiers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his reasoning, as רבא said: When we were at רב נחמן's house, when the seven days of פסח ended, he said to us: Go out and buy חמץ from the soldiers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to show that ruling like רבי שמעון, that חמץ after פסח can be permitted, fits רבא's own background.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids even a gentile's חמץ after פסח. רב נחמן let his students buy חמץ from gentiles immediately after פסח, which follows רבי שמעון. רבא learned this from his teacher, so his ruling like רבי שמעון is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Follows his own reasoning (is consistent)
The house (study hall) of רב נחמן
חמץ (Aramaic)
Soldiers (gentiles)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא rules like רבי שמעון after פסח, based on what he saw from his teacher רב נחמן.

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
When we were in the house of Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ נָפְקִי שִׁבְעָה יוֹמֵי דְפִסְחָא
phrases.english: when the seven days of Pesach went out,
he said to us: Go out and buy
chametz of the soldiers.
phrases.notes: Gentiles' חמץ, which was in existence during פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's ruling in step 1 that after פסח we follow רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling like רבי שמעון that חמץ after פסח is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's instruction to buy gentiles' חמץ right after פסח

steps.title: רב: pots used for חמץ on פסח must be broken
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that pots in which חמץ was cooked during פסח must be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Pots on פסח must be broken.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: רב rules about pots that absorbed חמץ during פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earthenware pots absorb taste and cannot be fully cleaned. Since the absorbed חמץ is forbidden במשהו, רב says the pots must be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Pots (earthenware)
Must be broken

phrases.english: Rav said: Pots on Pesach must be broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling, connected to רב's strict view on חמץ mixtures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pots that absorbed חמץ during פסח must be broken.

steps.title: Why not keep the pots for other foods after פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the pots must be broken. They could be kept until after פסח and used for foods of a different kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let him keep them until after פסח and cook in them food not of their kind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling as too strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רב agrees that after פסח, חמץ mixed with a different kind is permitted. So the pots could simply be used after פסח for other foods. Breaking them seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? (challenges a ruling)
Let him keep them (put them aside)

phrases.english: And why?
Let him keep them until after Pesach,
and cook in them something not of their kind!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement to break the pots
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After פסח, חמץ mixed into a different kind is permitted even according to רב, so the pots could be kept and used that way.

steps.title: A decree in case one cooks the same kind
steps.stepSummary: The pots must be broken because of a גזירה: a person might come to cook the same kind of food in them, which רב forbids even after פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest people come to cook in them food of the same kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule to break the pots is a protective rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that after פסח, חמץ mixed into the same kind is still forbidden במשהו. If the pots were kept, someone might forget and cook a grain dish in them. To prevent this, רב requires breaking them.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest they come to (do something forbidden)

steps.whatToRemember: Pots that absorbed חמץ on פסח are broken because of a גזירה, so no one cooks the same kind of food in them later.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 1 ruled like רבי שמעון that after פסח even the same kind is permitted. This answer is based on רב's own view, which forbids the same kind after פסח.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest they come
to cook in them food of its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה דִּילְמָא אָתוּ לְמֶיעְבַּד בְּהוּ בְּמִינוֹ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pots could be kept for foods of a different kind after פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: They must be broken as a safeguard, lest someone cook the same kind in them, which רב forbids.

steps.title: שמואל says the pots do not need to be broken
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב. The pots are kept until after פסח and may then be used for any food, even the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The pots are not broken. Instead, he keeps them until after פסח, and then he may cook in them food of the same kind or of a different kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's opinion, which argues with רב. שמואל says the pots do not need to be broken at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב required breaking the pots because of a גזירה that a person might cook the same kind of food in them. שמואל allows even the same kind of food after פסח. He holds like רבי שמעון that the taste of חמץ left over from פסח is permitted once פסח is over, so there is nothing to protect against.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not need to be broken
He keeps them (holds onto them)
After its time, meaning after פסח
Whether the same kind of food or a different kind

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not mean the pots may be used during פסח. He only allows them after פסח is over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic מחלוקת between רב and שמואל. רב is strict and requires breaking the pots. שמואל is lenient and allows everything after פסח.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
They are not to be broken,
rather, he keeps them until after its time (after Passover),
phrases.notes: זמנו = the time of the חמץ prohibition, meaning פסח.

phrases.english: and he prepares food in them
whether of the same kind or not of the same kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to רב's ruling, which was explained in Steps 5-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pots used for חמץ on פסח do not need to be broken. After פסח they may be used for any food, even the same kind.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent: his warning to the pot merchants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שמואל holds like רבי שמעון. He threatened the pot sellers that if they kept prices high, he would publicly rule like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning. שמואל said to the pot sellers: Make your prices fair for your pots. And if not, I will publicly teach you that the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל's lenient ruling fits his opinion elsewhere. It tells a story about him warning pot merchants who raised their prices after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Merchants raised prices because everyone needed new pots after פסח. If שמואל publicly ruled like רבי שמעון, people could keep using their old pots, and the merchants would lose business. The threat itself shows that שמואל truly holds like רבי שמעון, which matches his ruling in Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (is consistent with himself)
Pots or vessels
Make the prices fair (level the sale prices)
I will publicly teach or expound

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said to those who sell pots:
Make fair the prices of your pots,
and if not —
I will publicly teach for you like Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון permits benefiting from חמץ after פסח, so people could keep their old pots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's ruling in Step 8 by showing he holds like רבי שמעון elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's lenient ruling that the pots may be kept and used after פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's threat to the pot merchants that he would publicly rule like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Why didn't שמואל just teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, why only threaten? He should simply teach that ruling publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him teach it to them, since שמואל holds like רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. If שמואל really holds like רבי שמעון, why did he hold back his ruling and use it only as a threat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbi should teach the correct הלכה publicly whether or not merchants behave well. Keeping a true ruling hidden and using it only as a warning seems strange, so the גמרא asks for an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him teach it to them
He holds (this opinion)

phrases.english: But let him teach it to them,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: for Shmuel holds like Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִידְרוֹשׁ לְהוּ, דְּהָא שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story brought as proof in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's behavior of only threatening to teach like רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If שמואל truly holds like רבי שמעון, he should teach it outright instead of hiding it.

steps.title: It was רב's town
steps.stepSummary: שמואל did not teach openly because he was in רב's place, and רב disagreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. שמואל kept quiet because the town was under רב's authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out of respect, a rabbi does not publicly rule against the local authority in that authority's own place. Since רב forbids the pots, שמואל held back his lenient view. He was willing to make it public only to stop the merchants from overcharging.

keyTerms.meaning: רב's locale, the place where רב was the authority

steps.whatToRemember: רב: break the pots, because of a גזירה. שמואל: keep them and use them after פסח for anything, like רבי שמעון. שמואל held back his view only out of respect for רב in רב's town.

phrases.english: It was Rav's place.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Contextual or practical explanation (respect for the local authority)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, he should have taught it publicly.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held back out of respect for רב, because it was רב's town.

steps.title: The oven greased with meat fat
steps.stepSummary: An oven was smeared with meat fat. רבא בר אהילאי forbade eating bread baked in it forever, even with salt, in case someone eats it with a dairy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain oven that they smeared with fat. רבא בר אהילאי forbade eating bread from it, even with salt, forever, lest a person come to eat it with כותח (a dairy dip).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case. The meat taste soaked into the oven, and רבא בר אהילאי forbade all bread baked in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread itself is only meaty, so eating it plain or with salt would be fine. Still, he forbade it completely, because people might eat it with dairy and come to מאכל בשר בחלב. This is the same kind of protective גזירה as רב's ruling about the pots.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven
Fat or grease smeared on a surface
Bread
Salt
כותח, a dip made with milk
Lest he come to (a sign of a protective גזירה)

steps.confusionAlert: The bread is not forbidden because it is actually meat with milk. It is forbidden as a safeguard, because someone might eat it with dairy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב's style of reasoning, forbidding something completely to prevent a likely mistake, appears elsewhere in הלכה too.

phrases.english: There was a certain oven that they smeared with fat.
Rava bar Ahilai forbade it,
to eat the bread
even with salt, forever,
phrases.notes: לעולם: every bread baked in this oven is forbidden, not just the first batch.

phrases.english: lest he come to eat it with kutach (a dairy dip).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case of a protective גזירה, like רב's reasoning in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread baked in an oven greased with meat fat is forbidden forever, even with salt, lest it be eaten with dairy.

steps.title: A ברייתא is brought to challenge the ruling about the greased oven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises an objection to רבא בר אהילאי. It quotes a ברייתא: dough may not be kneaded with milk, and if it was, all the bread is forbidden because of the risk of habitual sin. The ברייתא then begins a similar case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: You may not knead dough with milk. If you did knead it with milk, the whole bread is forbidden, because it can lead to a sin people commit out of habit. Similarly...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge to רבא בר אהילאי by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the challenge. The part of the ברייתא that actually clashes with his ruling, a 'similar case' about an oven, comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread is normally eaten with anything, including meat. Bread kneaded with milk is a trap, because someone might eat it with meat and come to בשר בחלב, so the whole loaf is forbidden. The words 'כיוצא בו' tell us the ברייתא is about to apply the same idea to a parallel case. That case is a greased oven, the exact topic of רבא בר אהילאי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection: a challenge brought from a תנאי source (a משנה or ברייתא).
Knead (dough).
Dough.
A sin that comes from habit. People are used to eating bread with everything, so they might eat this milk bread with meat.
Similarly. It introduces a parallel case that follows the same rule.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the challenge is about the milk dough itself. The milk dough is just the first case of the ברייתא, and the two rulings agree that such bread is forbidden. The real point of attack is the parallel oven case that 'כיוצא בו' is about to introduce.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין לָשִׁין אֶת הָעִיסָּה בְּחָלָב,
phrases.english: They raised an objection: One may not knead the dough with milk,
phrases.notes: מיתיבי signals that a ברייתא is being quoted against the previous statement.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָשׁ — כׇּל הַפַּת כּוּלָּהּ אֲסוּרָה,
phrases.english: and if he kneaded it, all of the bread is entirely forbidden,
phrases.notes: Even after the fact, the whole loaf is forbidden.

phrases.english: because of a habitual transgression.
phrases.notes: People normally eat bread with meat, so they might eat this bread with meat and come to בשר בחלב.

phrases.english: Similarly,
phrases.notes: Setup: the parallel case, the greased oven, follows in the next lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵין לָשִׁין אֶת הָעִיסָּה בְּחָלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the ruling in step 12, that bread baked in an oven smeared with meat fat is forbidden forever.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר אהילאי's ruling that bread baked in an oven greased with fat is forbidden forever, even if eaten with salt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats milk dough and a greased oven as parallel cases (כיוצא בו). It continues on the next amud: if one greased an oven with fat, the bread is forbidden only until the oven is fired again (עד שיסיק את התנור). That clashes with רבא בר אהילאי's ruling that the bread is forbidden forever (לעולם).
